name: IT team · M1 demo-day rehearsal — prove the stack up at 09:00 before the 14:00 slot
description:
Context: M1 (`b9aaf03c`) runs its bring-up on 19 Nov; the demo slot is Fri **2026-11-21 14:00 Europe/Madrid** (go/no-go decided on `2506f948` at 12:00). No card owns the hours between "the stack was proven up on 19 Nov" and "management looks at it on 21 Nov". If the stack is down, the first person to find out is the audience. This card is the dry run.

DO, on the demo host, at 09:00 on 21 Nov — read-only with respect to product code:
1. Run the command sequence documented on `b9aaf03c`, verbatim, from the state a clean host would be in.
2. `docker compose ps` — every service must be `Up` / `healthy`. No `Exit`, no `Restarting`.
3. One HTTP status per URL claimed in `b9aaf03c`:
   `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' <url>` → expect `200`, or `301`/`302` to the login page.
4. Click the walkthrough: demo URL → login → workspace list renders → open one workspace. Screenshot with the URL visible.
5. Compare what you actually did against the demo script written on `b9aaf03c`. If it drifted, correct the script **on `b9aaf03c`**, not here.

IF THE STACK IS DOWN: restart and re-verify once. If it is still down, set this card `onhold`, post the **exact failing step and the error text** on both this card and `b9aaf03c`, and say "off track" in one line. Do not report "in progress".

IF `2506f948` resolved to Option C (no live audience): record the 5-minute walkthrough here, post the recording link plus the demo-script link on `b9aaf03c`, and close.

Acceptance: a comment with the verbatim 09:00 output (`docker compose ps` + HTTP codes + screenshot of login → workspace list) proving the stack is live for the 14:00 slot — or a named failing step with its error. No product-code change from this card; `up.sh` fixes belong to the M1 owner.

Why `devops`: this is the only profile with the host/docker/Compose access to bring the stack up and read container health. The PM runs the slot decision (`2506f948`) but does not execute the stack work.

Why `devops`: this is the only profile with the host/docker/Compose access to bring the stack up and read container health. The PM runs the slot decision (`2506f948`) but does not execute the stack work.

## PM ruling — 2026-11-19 shift: this card must end with an explicit GO / NO-GO

Two additions. Everything else in the description stands.

**1. Publish the verdict, not just the evidence.** The current acceptance ends with proof (`docker compose ps`, HTTP codes, screenshot) — but nobody is asked to *decide*. The demo starts four hours later with no named gate. So add a **final line in bold at the top of your comment**:
`GO — 14:00 slot confirmed` or `NO-GO — <the single failing step and its error>`.

Don't bury it in the evidence: the first line is the one that gets read.

**2. Clock check.** The slot is **14:00 Europe/Madrid = 13:00 UTC**; this card wakes 09:00 UTC (10:00 Madrid). That leaves ~3 hours of margin, not 5. If the bring-up needs a second attempt, take it, but report by 12:00 UTC whether it is GO or NO-GO so the fallback recording can start in time.

**On a NO-GO:** do not attempt fixes — `up.sh` changes belong to the M1 owner (`b9aaf03c`), and a rehearsal that starts editing the script invalidates itself. Record the failure verbatim, post it on `b9aaf03c`, and say *off track* in one line.

**What you are rehearsing, exactly:** the sequence frozen at the end of `b9aaf03c`'s 20 Nov 18:00 wake. If that sequence still contains `./up.sh --list-providers` without an exit-0 proof behind it, that is itself the NO-GO — say so rather than working around it.

## PM note — 2026-11-19 shift #5 (turn 3): your GO/NO-GO now has a consumer

Nothing about your instructions changes. One addition only: your verdict is now read by a named card, **`4f055e99`** (*M1 demo NO-GO branch*, wake **2026-11-21T10:30Z**, same `devops` profile, parent `2506f948`).

**Why it matters to you:** when you publish your one-liner, write the words **`GO`** or **`NO-GO`** literally, on the first line, in caps. Do not write "mostly fine", "should be OK", or "up with caveats" — the branch card keys off the word, and an ambiguous verdict leaves it unable to decide. If something is a caveat but the demo can still be run, say `GO` and then list the caveat.

**Sequence on 21 Nov, so you can see where you sit:**
- **09:00Z — you.** Bring the stack up on the demo host, publish `GO`/`NO-GO` with the command sequence and the evidence.
- 10:30Z — `4f055e99` acts on your word: on `GO` it closes in one line; on `NO-GO` it cancels the room, notifies management and proposes a replacement slot. It does **not** re-run your work.
- 11:00Z — `def4ce38` records the walkthrough (or the failure) as the evidence pack.
- 13:00Z — the 14:00 Madrid demo.

**Two things to keep in mind:** the demo script is frozen on commands that work today (`--list-providers` was removed on 19 Nov), so do not test flags that are not in the frozen sequence — `2639c296` and `3ba4772f` are off this path deliberately. And if the bring-up fails, report the failure rather than retrying repeatedly: one documented failure plus evidence is what unblocks the next shift.

## Two corrections before your 09:00Z wake: your seat can do this, and one of your standing instructions is now stale.

### 1. Assignment fixed — step 4 was unachievable as written
Profiles are now **`devops` + `qa_explorer`** (was `devops` alone). Verified from the profile definitions, not assumption:
- `devops` → `docker_ps`, `docker_compose_service`, `docker_exec`, `docker_stats`, `traefik` ⇒ your steps 1, 2, 3.
- `qa_explorer` → `start_session`, `browse_action`, `get_screenshot`, `browser_control` ⇒ your step 4 (demo URL → login → workspace list → open one workspace, screenshot with the URL visible).
- **No seat has a host shell.** So `bash -n demo/up.sh` and a host-side `./up.sh` invocation are not runnable by any agent here: use `docker_exec` into a container that has the repo mounted. If that is genuinely impossible, name the exact command you could not run and mark it as the human operator's step on `b9aaf03c`. One unrunnable command does not make the stack unverifiable — do not collapse the whole rehearsal into "no shell available".

### 2. Your `--list-providers` instruction is stale
Your last comment says the flag was removed on 19 Nov and `2639c296` is off this path deliberately. **That changed at 11:28Z today:** `2639c296` implemented `--list-providers` and `--ref` (`demo/up.sh` +45/−2). The flag now **exists but has never been executed anywhere**.

So do this, and keep it out of the frozen sequence:
- Run `./up.sh --list-providers` **outside** the demo sequence, expect exit 0 and the 8 presets.
- If it works → comment **"upgrade line 3 of the sequence to `--list-providers`"**. That is the one and only permitted change on demo day, and it must be made before 13:00Z.
- If it fails → comment **"keep `--help`"** and change nothing. The demo does not depend on it either way.

### 3. Test the tree that will be shown
`b9aaf03c` freezes the sequence at 18:00Z on 20 Nov and records the commit plus `project_changes(paths=["demo/"], scope="all")`. Paste the same two values next to your results. If they differ from the frozen ones, **stop and say so** — you would be rehearsing a different tree from the one management will see, and that is precisely the failure this card exists to prevent.

Ignore the stale line in your own description ("go/no-go decided on `2506f948` at 12:00"): the chain is now 12:00Z on 20 Nov (conditional) → 09:00Z you → 10:30Z `4f055e99` → 11:00Z `def4ce38` → 13:00Z demo. Your `GO` / `NO-GO` one-liner at 09:00 remains the single input `4f055e99` acts on.
